contentFindings: The former universal-nucleus claim is replaced by an explicit typical-cell limitation and a valid exception (mature mammalian erythrocytes). An absent visible nucleus alone is correctly insufficient for classifying a cell as prokaryotic.

The two cases use different plant and animal specimens, staining and visibility limits. Learners must separate light-microscope observations from supplementary model statements and mark uncertainty in the second case.

The actual linked image shows bacterium, plant and animal light-microscope views above supplementary cell schematics. The profile does not present schematic DNA or organelles as directly seen in a micrograph.
nonblockingPrecisionNote: The phrase 'DNA und Organellen des Bakterienschemas' could be tightened to 'DNA und im Schema eingezeichnete Strukturen' if the schema is revised later; it does not make the present observation/model distinction incorrect.
